interactions.title: Recap: the Mystai, Grash, and Shakun’s missing heart
lines: DM: Since leaving Karawa, you've learned of the Order of the Awakened Soul, the Mystai of Bhishma, who since the Great War have dedicated themselves to finding the unburied dead in the desolation of Cha'mutte and putting them to rest. You also learned that these same monks, 30 years ago, embarked on a mission somehow involving the great mage Rai to close the portal or cleanse the land or heal evil somehow. Seem to have failed.

DM: According to Karmana, the ghost of the last master of the Bhishma Mystai, um, who remained behind to protect the monastery, since this failure evil has been growing slowly across the land. Until last summer, when darkness arrived in Kharsan in the form of Grash the Blighted One. Grash, now apparently the master and commander of an ever-growing clan of orcs, is bent on, on war, at least for now against Uzgash's horde, an apparently peaceful clan of orcs living somewhere along one of the desert rivers, farming and keeping to themselves.

DM: While exploring the monastery, you also discovered the still-divine passageway to the initiation rituals of the Bhishma Mystai, which Kenzo and Seeker followed. Well, at the end Seeker turned away. Kenzo committed to becoming a Mystai and learning that Shakun, the daughter of Bhishma and Laka, was present with her parents, as always, in the realm of Arkash, the spiritual plane of the Five Siblings. But she could not reach the world, cannot reach Karawa, could not reach her temple there to power the mystical protections of Dunmar, because their heart, a red ochre stone imbued with her divine essence, was missing.

DM: Turning from the initiation halls to explore the hall of stories, you learn some of the history of the Bhishma Mystai, the conflicts and decisions leading up to the fateful attempt to close a portal, heal the land, cure evil somehow. And the involvement of Rai, initially connected to the Mystai through Drankor, possibly the portal to another plane there.

interactions.title: Grash executes his servants and sends the shadows hunting
lines: DM: Okay, so so Seeker, let me, let me tell you what you see first. So, so, remember, you can pick hearing or or vision, but you can switch between them.

DM: So as the sensor appears, you see—you—your sensor appears in a large room, mostly dark, lit only by torches that line the wall, casting flickering shadows, you know, across the room. The—the windows have been bricked up and the—and the second story and third story of this building have been knocked out, so there's this one room that goes up maybe 35–40 feet tall. All the window is covered in stone, so it's completely dark. There's no light that gets in.

DM: The... On the ground, you see this looks like it was once a—an audience chamber, throne room type of deal. There is a—there is, like a dais at the far, dais at the far end that's raised up a few steps. There's debris as if, like old furniture has been cast aside. And there is just a plain—like dark black metal, possibly metal from a distance it's hard—from, you know, from this perspective it’s hard to say. Just a simple black chair sitting on this raised platform, and seated in the, middle metal chair—the—a skeletal creature, maybe seven foot tall, um, wearing chainmail armor. Resting against the—against the back of the throne is a wicked-looking glaive with a blade that sort of etched in, with like—like, it almost looks like it's been sort of [garbled], so it's got this jagged, jagged edge. This skeletal creature is sitting in this throne, looking intently at two orcs that are kneeling on the ground, like bow down entirely on the, throne—on the ground, and in front of this this chair, um, and he seems to be saying something quietly to them.
DM: So you use your scroll, and suddenly, mid-sentence, the the Orcish becomes becomes clear to you. And this creature sitting on the throne is saying, ‘For the last—’

DM: Ah, yes. ‘My name is Grash, and here is my secret plan.’ No, he says, ‘For the last time. First gnolls, now whoever these intruders were, humans, elves. I will not have more incursions into my city. Stand. Bow your head.’ And the orcs kind of look at each other and they stand up, and he takes this glaive and he walks towards them, and with one swing cleaves both of their heads straight from their shoulders.
